observations.statement: MS-001 is an accepted migration-lineage-only compatibility disposition; it no longer owns product coverage, which is assigned to MS-002 through MS-106 or explicit structural, retired, and migration-coverage dispositions.

The retired bridge uses source_preserving_bridge_retired mode with WorkNode creation disabled, and its acceptance criteria prohibit WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, and production build tasks.
Migration coverage names two validation commands and four run-scoped proof artifacts.

Models_System owns provider/model precedence, availability, and selection; Executor, WorktreeGitImprovement, orchestrator-subagent-integration, and Crosswalk are consumers that must not define independent precedence rules.
Dispatch-time carry-through must preserve requested and effective provider/model identity without creating a second precedence owner.

For Goal Runtime, Models_System owns concrete requested/effective resolution and capability evidence for worker, planner, evaluator, verifier, and adjudicator, while Goal_Runtime_System owns block/degrade semantics and provider-specific default tier mappings remain deferred.
Goal Runtime role policies must be able to request resolution for five named roles, expose requested/effective identity and capability evidence where relevant, and avoid hard-coded provider defaults.

Orchestrator resolution takes capability_lane and agent_role bindings, names six required lane roles, and must use configured providers, accounts, model profiles, and provider-specific owner documents.

A missing required binding must yield an unconfigured-lane blocker rather than an arbitrary default, while requested/effective identity and capability evidence feed runtime receipts and GUI projections.
Legacy tier labels are compatibility/search aliases; write_mode and certification_tier remain references to other owner surfaces rather than Models-owned enforcement or certification semantics.

MS-110 defines six user-facing model settings whose responsibilities cover default chat/research/fallback, planning and compilation oversight, normal implementation, GUI/frontend work, high-effort work, and auditing/certification.
The Auditor loop repeats audit, bounded repair, and re-audit until certification or a critical block or authority boundary, while Executor remains deterministic and has no user-facing model setting.
MS-110 acceptance fixes the setting count, maps planning/compiler conversions to Overseer, retires legacy validation-pass selectors and stages, and keeps Executor model-free.

The adjacent post-core context begins MS-111 and names a model-resolution receipt field set and routing metadata, including requested/effective model profiles, fallback facts, capability checks, and capability-lane metadata.

candidate_findings.title: Provider/model precedence lacks a deterministic resolution algorithm
candidate_findings.statement: MS-107 declares ownership of precedence and requires requested/effective identity preservation, while MS-109 names multiple configured selection sources, but the core does not order those sources or specify tie-breaking and fallback eligibility when more than one valid binding exists.
candidate_findings.impact: Different consumers can choose different effective providers or models for the same inputs while all claim conformance, making receipts and GUI projections non-reproducible.

candidate_findings.title: Capability evidence and blocker behavior are not typed
candidate_findings.statement: MS-108 makes capability evidence conditional with the phrase where relevant, and MS-109 requires unconfigured-lane blockers, but the core defines neither capability evidence dimensions and pass/fail rules nor blocker payload, status, and retry or recovery transitions.
candidate_findings.impact: Resolvers and consumers cannot reliably agree on eligibility, distinguish terminal from recoverable failures, or validate that blocking behavior is correct.

candidate_findings.title: The required capability-lane role set is not closed
candidate_findings.statement: The six lane roles are introduced with the word include, but the core gives no closed registry, extension authority, versioning rule, or behavior for an unknown agent_role or capability_lane.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders may disagree about which bindings are mandatory and whether unknown or newly added roles block dispatch.

candidate_findings.title: Overlapping model-setting routes have no precedence
candidate_findings.statement: MS-110 assigns Worker, GUI / Frontend Worker, High-Effort Worker, Auditor, and Overseer using work characteristics and activities that can overlap, but it provides no priority or tie-break contract for a request matching multiple categories.
candidate_findings.impact: The same GUI, high-risk, broad, validation-heavy, or supervision-related request can be routed to different user-configured models by different implementations.

candidate_findings.title: The Auditor loop lifecycle is incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: The audit-to-repair loop names high-level stop conditions but does not define loop states, bounded-repair limits, retry ceiling or backoff, cancellation, idempotency, concurrent-run behavior, or the evidence predicate for completion certification.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can loop indefinitely, duplicate repairs, race concurrent audits, or certify completion using incompatible evidence thresholds.

candidate_findings.title: Behavioral acceptance is deferred or manual
candidate_findings.statement: Across MS-107 through MS-110, validation surfaces are plan-index or schema gates plus manual or future reviews; the core provides no executable oracle for precedence outcomes, blocker behavior, routing collisions, or loop termination.
candidate_findings.impact: Accepted PlanUnit metadata can validate while the consequential runtime and GUI-facing behavior remains unproven.

candidate_findings.title: User-facing model-setting states are underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: MS-110 owns six user-facing settings and their labels and routing roles, but its acceptance criteria do not define allowed value domains, empty or unconfigured and error states, persistence and update behavior, fallback disclosure, or accessibility behavior; FinalGUISpec is only named as an implementation surface here.
candidate_findings.impact: Settings implementations can expose inconsistent controls and feedback and cannot be tested against a complete user-visible state contract from this PlanUnit.

candidate_findings.title: The advanced-override exception lacks authority
candidate_findings.statement: The exactly-six setting rule is qualified by unless a later advanced override is accepted, but the core names no accepting authority, compatibility or migration rule, or evidence required for that exception.
candidate_findings.impact: The public setting contract can be widened without a deterministic governance decision or migration path.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: MS-001 retirement and the transfer of product coverage away from the bridge are explicit.
The retired bridge compile mode and prohibition on WorkNode and build-task creation are explicit.
Migration validation commands and proof-artifact paths are named rather than left wholly implicit.
Provider/model precedence ownership and the named consumer boundary are explicit, including the prohibition on a second precedence owner.

Goal_Runtime_System ownership of block/degrade semantics is explicit, and Models_System is prohibited from hard-coding provider defaults or collapsing verifier/adjudicator roles into the worker selection.
Missing required lane bindings explicitly block as unconfigured-lane instead of silently selecting an arbitrary default.
Legacy tier wording is explicitly non-canonical, and Models_System is explicitly excluded from write_mode enforcement, worktree lease policy, and certification semantics.
The six setting labels and the absence of a user-facing Executor Model are explicit.
Legacy validation_pass_report and Pass 1 / Pass 2 / Pass 3 names are explicitly limited to lineage or compatibility aliases rather than active selectors or stages.
The Auditor loop has explicit high-level terminal categories: completion certification, critical block, and authority boundary.
The adjacent context prevents treating receipt field naming as wholly absent by enumerating requested/effective profiles, fallback facts, capability checks, and routing metadata.
The stale Plan Wizard conversation token is explicitly identified as legacy while current prose uses Planning Wizard.

unknowns.statement: Provider-specific default tier mappings are explicitly deferred, so their future owner, values, and activation conditions are unknown in this window.
The phrase where relevant does not identify which Goal Runtime roles require capability evidence or when evidence may be omitted.
It is unknown whether the six named required lane roles are exhaustive or extensible and who can add another role.
The winning source and tie-break order are unknown when several configured providers, accounts, model profiles, or provider-owner rules can satisfy one binding.
The identity of the certifying authority and the evidence threshold behind completion is certified are not stated in the core.
The accepting authority and lifecycle for a later advanced override to the six-setting rule are unknown.

Selector control types, defaults, edit and persistence behavior, error presentation, fallback disclosure, and accessibility behavior are not stated here even though FinalGUISpec is an implementation surface.

The adjacent context names receipt fields but does not establish their types, required or optional status, nullability, persistence lifecycle, or capability_checks schema within the available context range.

Models_System owns the six user-facing model settings for plans-to-code automation: Default Model, Overseer Model, Worker Model, GUI / Frontend Worker Model, High-Effort Worker Model, and Auditor Model. Default Model covers assistant chat, normal Planning Wizard conversation, ordinary research/browser lookup, and fallback behavior. Overseer Model covers Planning Wizard ledger-to-Plans conversion, PRD Builder structured conversion, Plans-to-WorkNode-request compilation, seam/split/merge decisions, execution supervision, graph patch recommendations, and blocked-state reasoning. Worker Model handles normal WorkNode implementation; GUI / Frontend Worker Model handles GUI/frontend/UX/layout/visual WorkNodes; High-Effort Worker Model handles difficult, broad, repo-wide, high-risk, or high-reasoning WorkNodes; Auditor Model owns the Auditor audit-to-repair loop, verification, certification, quality gates, and evidence review. The loop repeats audit, bounded repair, and re-audit, also recorded by the legacy source token audit/repair/audit, until completion is certified or a critical block or authority boundary stops the loop. Executor has no user-facing Executor Model setting because Executor is deterministic scheduler/runtime machinery and Overseer handles execution-level reasoning around it.
  High-Effort Worker Model covers repo-wide reasoning explicitly, and Executor deterministic runtime behavior stays outside user-facing model settings.

Every dispatched WorkNode and every plans-to-code role resolution records a model resolution receipt with requested_lane, requested_model_profile, effective_model_profile, fallback_used, fallback_reason, and capability_checks. WorkNode requests carry work_type, gui_related, frontend_related, effort class, reasoning tier, context size, validation cost, risk class, authority risk, user-visible risk, and capability lane metadata so native routing can choose Worker Model, GUI / Frontend Worker Model, High-Effort Worker Model, Auditor Model, or Overseer Model without exposing Codex-only external GUI-agent CLI bridge settings in built Puppet Master.
  The receipt is the native provider/model routing proof for built Puppet Master and preserves effort_class and capability_lane in the canonical routing body.
